Real exam mechanics are PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY HEDGED. CONFIRMED directly and explicitly from Wyoming's own manual text (Section i -- Wyoming Information, page i.ii): "All written tests are multiple choice. The passing score for a written test is 80 percent," consistent with the federally standardized minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a); this 80% figure was independently re-confirmed against the current live WYDOT CDL Testing page (https://www.dot.state.wy.us/home/driver_license_records/commercial-license/commercial_testing.html, checked 2026-08-24), which states the identical passing-score language. HEDGED: the exact number of items per knowledge test (General Knowledge or any endorsement test) is never disclosed anywhere in the fetched official Wyoming manual text -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for "questions," "items," and similar terms, which surfaced no per-test item-count table -- and this absence was independently re-confirmed on both the live CDL Testing page and the live CDL Class Information page (https://www.dot.state.wy.us/home/driver_license_records/commercial-license/commercial_testing/cdl-class-information.html), neither of which states a question count for any test. No item count is asserted as an officially confirmed Wyoming figure anywhere in this question bank. A minor discrepancy was found and is flagged rather than silently resolved: the Oct 2024 manual states the CDL skills test fee is $80, while the live CDL Testing webpage (checked 2026-08-24) states $85 -- likely a fee increase since the manual's printing; this bank cites the manual's own $80 figure since that is the text being sourced for provenance. Other Wyoming-specific mechanics confirmed directly from the manual: a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) is valid for 365 days and must be held at least 14 days before skills testing; the CDL skills test consists of a vehicle pre-trip inspection, a basic control skills test, and an on-the-road skills test, conducted by appointment only, with the applicant furnishing the test vehicle; an additional $5 technology fee applies to all driver license classes and CDL skills tests; ELDT (Entry Level Driver Training) has been required since February 7, 2022 for a first Class A/B CDL, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first School Bus/Passenger/Hazmat endorsement; Wyoming defines 18 restriction codes (A through Z, effective 07/01/2024: A, B, C, D, E, G, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, R, V, X, Z); a CLP may only carry Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsements (each requiring a paired restriction), and a Tanker (N) CLP endorsement must carry an X no-cargo-in-tank restriction; hazmat endorsement (H or X) renewal requires in-person appearance with TSA background-check paperwork, and out-of-state CDL transfers with an H endorsement must retake the Wyoming hazmat knowledge test. Wyoming's manual has a genuine, deliberate structural quirk (not a duplication error) that shaped this bank's bucket design: it prints BOTH the original AAMVA-format Section 11 (Pre-trip Vehicle Inspection Test) and Section 12 (Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test) AND their "Modernized" replacements, Section 11M and Section 12M, describing the SAME underlying inspection/skills content in two different presentation formats (11M/12M use a "Description / Why Inspect / Inspection" or explicit scoring-rule format; 11/12 use terser prose) -- reflecting that WYDOT examiners use either format depending on the testing day. This bank's 13_vehicle_inspection bucket draws from the union of Sections 11 and 11M without near-duplicating the same fact twice, preferring 11M's fuller "Why Inspect" reasoning where it adds depth; the 14_basic_control_onroad bucket similarly merges Sections 12, 12M (including its detailed pull-up/back-up/encroachment/look scoring rules), and 13 On-Road Driving. Content-depth rationale: Wyoming uses the same AAMVA-authored base manual structure as several other CDL-track states in this project, organized into the same 13 core sections plus Wyoming-specific front matter -- Section i Wyoming Information (licensing requirements, restriction codes, ELDT, required tests, fees, license services, traffic-stop procedures) combined with Section 1 Introduction into the licensing bucket; Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers); Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely; Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely; Section 5 Air Brakes; Section 6 Combination Vehicles; Section 7 Doubles and Triples; Section 8 Tank Vehicles; Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.7 Hazardous Materials Emergencies -- explicitly excluding the 9.8 Glossary, since the manual states in a parenthetical note "You will not be tested on this glossary"); Section 10 School Buses (rich in genuinely Wyoming-specific content, including direct citations to Wyoming Statutes W.S. 31-5-929(b) and W.S. 31-5-507(b) for school-bus warning-light and roadway-position rules); and the combined Sections 11/11M Vehicle Inspection Test and 12/12M/13 Basic Control Skills/On-Road Driving buckets described above. Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 20 questions, Tank Vehicles: 16, Doubles/Triples: 24) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (135 across two buckets, including a supplemental pass adding 10 questions on the manual's substantial but initially under-drafted Fatigue and Lack of Alertness content under subsection 2.11), Hazardous Materials (100 across two buckets), Combination Vehicles (60), Air Brakes (55), and School Bus (55) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than a fixed per-bucket target. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Wyoming manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake psi thresholds, tank-endorsement gallon thresholds of 119/1,000 gallons, school-bus danger-zone and mirror blind-spot distances, railroad-crossing stop distances, hazmat placarding thresholds, fatigue/drowsy-driving statistics) were verified against the actual Wyoming text read during drafting.
